description: Coding agents' CLIs - and your own - in their own terminal UIs inside the window, with an MCP server through which agents start, list and stop each other.
config.title: Agents
config.yolo: YOLO for the agents you start. On, an agent's CLI runs with its sandbox off and asks for nothing. Off, its sandbox is on where the CLI has one, and it asks before its own commands and edits - but never before a call of Facade's tools. An agent keeps the YOLO it started with, and the agents it starts take it.
config.enabled: The agent framework: agents start, list and stop agents through Facade's tools. Off, your agents start, run and end as before, without Facade's tools.
config.timeout: How many seconds Facade waits on what it does not control: a new agent to connect to it, an agent's process to end once stopped, this window for an agent's MCP server, and the terminals a reload gives back.
config.launch.arguments: Command-line arguments, group by group, in this order: `warmUp`, `connect`, `quiet`, `questions`, `messages`, `yoloOn`, `yoloOff`, `model`, `effort`, `extra` (your own), `task`. A group you set replaces Facade's; `null` leaves it out. `yoloOn` is given only while YOLO is on and `yoloOff` only while it is off; `warmUp`, `connect` and `messages` only with the agent framework on; `model`, `effort` and `task` only when an agent gives them. Facade fills in `${folder}`, `${repository}` (its main checkout), `${home}`, `${messagesDir}`, `${model}`, `${effort}`, `${task}` and the like for each agent.
config.launch.environment: Environment variables Facade sets for each agent. One you set replaces Facade's; `null` removes one of Facade's.
config.launch.unattended: What an agent started through `start_agent` - by another agent, or by your script - runs with in place of the launch, so that nothing waits for an answer while nobody may be watching: its `arguments` groups replace the launch's groups of the same name, and its `environment` and `settings` go over the launch's. An agent you start from the agent menu runs with the launch alone.
config.launch.unattended.arguments: Argument groups for an agent started through `start_agent`, each in place of the launch's group of the same name. A group you set replaces Facade's; `null` gives that agent none of the group.
config.launch.unattended.environment: Environment variables for an agent started through `start_agent`, over the launch's. One you set replaces Facade's; `null` removes one, the launch's too.
config.launch.unattended.settings: Claude Code's settings for an agent started through `start_agent`, merged over the launch's key by key; `null` removes a key, the launch's too.
config.launch.trust: What Facade does wherever an agent starts, so that the CLI does not stop to ask whether you trust the folder - its whole repository: `arguments` given for that run, or `merge` written into the CLI's own `file`, where it stays. `null`: Facade gives no trust, and the CLI asks in its terminal.
config.launch.enterDelay: Milliseconds between typing a line into the agent's terminal and pressing Enter: the CLI may take fast typing for a paste.
config.launch.taskDelay: Milliseconds after the agent's CLI connects to Facade before the line that gives its task is typed into its terminal - for a CLI that gets its task that way.
config.claude.launch.settings: Claude Code settings for each agent, on top of yours, key by key; `null` removes one of Facade's. One value of a kind Claude Code does not take makes it ignore all of them.
config.claude.title: Claude Code
config.claude.enabled: Offer Claude Code in the agent menu and to agents.
config.claude.path: The Claude Code program to run. Leave it empty to use `claude` from your PATH.
config.claude.launch: How Facade starts Claude Code. Write only what you change: in settings.json, choose a part inside the braces to fill in Facade's own, then change it; `null` removes one of Facade's. **Agents: Show Agent Launch** shows what each agent is started with now.

config.custom.title: Custom Agents
config.custom: Your own agents, by name: `{ "<name>": { "path": "...", "launch": { ... } } }`. Each is started as a built-in is, in a terminal of its own. Its launch has the parts of a built-in's - its arguments group by group, environment, trust and delays - and Facade fills in none of them: a group you leave out adds nothing. In arguments, `${mcpConfig}` names a file with Facade's MCP server in the `mcpServers` form, for your `connect` group, and `${folder}`, `${repository}`, `${home}`, `${messagesDir}`, `${model}`, `${effort}` and `${task}` are filled in as for a built-in.
config.custom.path: The program to run: a file, or a command on the PATH a terminal gets.
config.custom.launch: How Facade starts it, part by part, as a built-in's launch: only the groups you fill in are given.
